questions.q: In a running show, which key sequence jumps directly to slide number 7?
questions.solution: Type the slide number and press Enter to jump straight there during a show (works up to the deck's length).
questions.shortcut: Type-and-Enter is the show's hidden navigator; Home/End only reach first/last.

questions.q: Which function displays the current date that updates every time the workbook recalculates?
questions.solution: =TODAY() returns the live current date (updating on recalculation); =NOW() adds the time as well; =DATE() builds a date from given year/month/day; Ctrl+D fills down, it does not insert a date.
questions.shortcut: 'Date only, updating' -> TODAY(); 'date and time' -> NOW(); 'fixed stamp' -> Ctrl+;.

questions.q: Restarting a computer without switching off the power is called:
questions.solution: Warm booting (restart) reloads the OS without removing power. Cold booting means starting from a fully powered-off state.
questions.shortcut: Warm = restart (machine stays 'warm'); cold = switch on from off.

questions.q: The formula =SUM(A1:A5, 10) is entered in B1. A1:A5 contain 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. The result is:
questions.solution: SUM adds the range (2+4+6+8+10 = 30) plus the extra argument 10, giving 40.
questions.shortcut: SUM takes every argument: range total first, then any loose numbers.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Please **revert back** to my mail by Friday.
questions.solution: **Revert** already means 'come back' → the echo *back* is redundant: 'please **revert to** my mail'. 'Reverting to' breaks the request form; the original keeps the echo.
questions.shortcut: revert, return, repeat — cut the echo word.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The flight was cancelled ___ the dense fog over the airport.
questions.solution: Fog is the cause, and a noun phrase ('the dense fog') follows, so **because of** is needed. 'Because' needs a full clause, and 'although' and 'despite' express contrast, not cause.
questions.shortcut: Cause + noun -> because of / owing to.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Grandmother looks ___ the baby while the parents are at work.
questions.solution: Caring for someone is **looking after** them. 'Look into' means investigate, 'look for' means search, 'look up' means find in a book or visit.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (3).
questions.solution: The contrast inside the quote: a ___ player who studies ONE game a day beats one who plays ten games CARELESSLY. The winning quality is **patient** study — the opposite of careless speed. *Wealthy*, *noisy* and *absent* have nothing to do with how one studies a game.
questions.shortcut: Find the stated opposite (careless) and choose the word on the other pole.
questions.passage: Every Sunday, Farida sets up chessboards in the park behind the market and teaches whoever stops to watch. What began as a pastime has become a small (1) ______: forty children from the nearby lanes attend her free class. She insists that chess does not (2) ______ talent alone; it rewards habit. 'A (3) ______ player who studies one game a day will soon beat a player who plays ten games carelessly,' she says. The market traders, who once asked her to move away, now (4) ______ room for her boards every Sunday morning.

questions.q: Which of the following received the **Bharat Ratna in 1954**, the first year of the award?
questions.solution: The 1954 recipients were **C. Rajagopalachari, S. Radhakrishnan and C.V. Raman**. Nehru got it in 1955; Ambedkar and Patel received it posthumously in 1990 and 1991.

questions.q: Tulsidas composed the ***Ramcharitmanas*** in which language?
questions.solution: *Ramcharitmanas* (16th century) is in **Awadhi**. Surdas wrote *Sursagar* in Braj Bhasha; Vidyapati wrote in Maithili.

questions.q: The temperate grasslands of Argentina are known as:
questions.solution: The **Pampas** are the temperate grasslands of **Argentina** (and Uruguay). Prairies are in North America, Steppes in Eurasia and Downs in Australia.

questions.q: The city of **Agra** was founded in 1504 by —
questions.solution: **Sikandar Lodi** founded Agra and made it his second capital. He also introduced the **Gaz-i-Sikandari**, a standard measuring yard.

questions.q: Find the value of $1 \div \left(1 + \cfrac{1}{1 + \cfrac{1}{1 + \cfrac{1}{2}}}\right)$
questions.shortcut: The whole $1 + \frac{1}{\dots}$ block sits under the first division.

questions.q: The LCM of two co-prime numbers is 221. If one of them is 13, find the other number.
questions.solution:
Co-prime numbers have HCF 1, so LCM = product.
Other number $= \frac{221}{13} = 17$.

questions.q: Point $P$ is at a distance of $13$ cm from the centre $O$ of a circle of radius $5$ cm. The length of the tangent drawn from $P$ to the circle is:
questions.figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 250 175" width="250" stroke="currentColor" fill="none"><circle cx="65" cy="105" r="50"/><line x1="65" y1="105" x2="185" y2="105" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/><line x1="185" y1="105" x2="85.8" y2="59.5"/><line x1="65" y1="105" x2="85.8" y2="59.5"/><text x="65" y="105" dx="-14" dy="6" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="14" font-family="sans-serif">O</text><text x="185" y="105" dx="2" dy="16" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="14" font-family="sans-serif">P</text><text x="85.8" y="59.5" dx="-4" dy="-6" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="14" font-family="sans-serif">T</text></svg>
questions.solution: The radius to the point of contact is perpendicular to the tangent: $PT^2=OP^2-OT^2=169-25=144$, so $PT=12$ cm.

questions.q: A bag contains 50-paise, 25-paise and 10-paise coins in the ratio 5 : 9 : 4, amounting to ₹103 in all. The number of 10-paise coins is:

A survey of **100 people** on how they get news — Newspaper (N), TV (T) and Radio (R) — gave these region counts:

- Only N: 20 · Only T: 25 · Only R: 5
- N and T only: 15 · T and R only: 6 · N and R only: 4
- All three: 10 · None of the three: 15

How many people use the **newspaper or the radio but not TV**?
questions.solution: Regions in N or R and outside T: only N 20 + only R 5 + N-R only 4 = **29**. 25 forgets the N-R region; 39 wrongly adds the all-three region, which contains TV watchers.
questions.shortcut: Remove every region that touches T.

questions.q: How many squares are there in the given figure?
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 64 64" width="64" height="64" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><line x1="5" y1="5" x2="5" y2="59"/><line x1="23" y1="5" x2="23" y2="59"/><line x1="41" y1="5" x2="41" y2="59"/><line x1="59" y1="5" x2="59" y2="59"/><line x1="5" y1="5" x2="59" y2="5"/><line x1="5" y1="23" x2="59" y2="23"/><line x1="5" y1="41" x2="59" y2="41"/><line x1="5" y1="59" x2="59" y2="59"/></svg>
questions.solution: 1 × 1 squares: 9. 2 × 2 squares: 4. 3 × 3 square: 1. Total 9 + 4 + 1 = **14**.

questions.q: Find the odd one out: **8, 27, 64, 100**
questions.solution: 8 = 2³, 27 = 3³, 64 = 4³ are cubes; 100 lies between 4³ = 64 and 5³ = 125, and is not a cube → **100**.
questions.shortcut: Cube roots to 10 by heart; check the gap between neighbouring cubes.

questions.q:
In the following series, one number is **wrong**. Find the wrong number.

**2, 10, 4, 13, 6, 16, 9, 19**
questions.solution: Odd places: 2, 4, 6, **8** (+2). Even places: 10, 13, 16, 19 (+3). The 7th term shows 9 instead of 8 → **9**.
questions.shortcut: Split the series; the error hides in one half.
